text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Cooling Pad N200 with USB-Powered 2-Speed Fan The Logitech Cooling Pad N200 is a simple padded platform your laptop rests on to keep the hot underside of the laptop from roasting your legs. It connects to the laptop with a USB plug, and draws power from the laptop to run a 2-speed cooling fan (controlled by a switch located on the USB plug).

The pad works splendidly. The fan makes only minor noise in operation even at the highest speed (no more noise than the laptop's own fans make when they engage), and I am completely protected from the heat from the underside of the laptop. The bottom of the pad is nicely padded and is comfortable in use. I didn't have to adjust my position at any point, as I often have to do with the laptop alone, when I need to shift the underside's "hot spot" to another area of my legs.

I can't speak to how much this drains the laptop battery since I very rarely use my laptop without having it plugged in via an AC adapter (my laptop battery is failing and can't run for long without being plugged into the wall).

If I had one nitpick, I would suggest to Logitech that future models have some sort of attachment feature that would allow the laptop to be securely attached to the pad. At present the laptop just rests on top of pad, with the USB connector serving as the only connection between the laptop and the pad. I'd like them to be more securely attached to one another so it's less cumbersome to carry the laptop to another room. But that is a minor issue, and I am otherwise very pleased with this.

Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Cooling Pad N200 with USB-Powered 2-Speed Fan

HUANUO Dual Monitor Arm for 13 to 27 inch, Gas Spring Monitor Stands for 2 Monitors Vesa Mount with Clamp/Grommet Base, Computer Dual Monitor Desk Mount for up to 17.6 lbs per Arm At the current price tag, I am pretty amazed at these, considering the other type I have is (or more likely was) closer to $300. The other had a well-established brand name, although I don't actually remember what it was. They are actually pretty similar, with the other having decent instructions, feeling just slightly more solid, and better cable management overall.

They both have to be messed with, tightened, and tweaked to get them to work the way you want them to. Thankfully, I don't need either to be constantly moved, but constant re-positioning will be challenging on either stand. Both of them, you don't have to put a hole in your desk. You also need to be very careful (with both of them) to position your cables with just the right amount of slack so that they don't look stupid, but have enough slack to reposition when necessary without stretching the cables.

I like to use two small TVs to use as monitors and run 2 no-nonsense (i.e., thin) HDMI cables, coax, an audio cable, and the power to each. That way, you can set the desk up to accommodate two different docking stations. Don't forget Ethernet if the TVs are smart (mine are not, but they have PIP). If you really take your time, you can fit all that stuff in, and hopefully never have to re-run cables, because it is sort of a pain (but well worth it). Get black cables to match.

As it is, I have no desire to either replace the glass, or worse, buy a new iPad, so I got the super functional, heavy duty case. The iPad doesn't look as pretty in it, and the screen often looks dirty or smudged as the built-in screen protector doesn't keep it as clean looking as the stick on sheets, but it definitely does it's job.

While I like the hinge covers for the back camera and the speakers, they aren't very little kid friendly. It's easy for the kids to pull them out, and putting them back requires taking the iPad out of the case, replacing the hinged covers, then going through the effort of putting the iPad back. After doing that once, I just leave them off now. I wish there was no way for them to come off, but it isn't a deal breaker for me.

Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation I have some cognitive impairment and mobility challenges from lupus, and I was able to set up Fire TV really easily. The batteries go in the remote; the hdmi cable goes where it goes, and the power plugs in where it plugs in. The interface is simple and intuitive, and you can get everywhere with the home button, the directionals, back, and select. The only painful part for me/my hands was logging into my wireless network via the onscreen qwerty keyboard.

The screens are responsive with virtually no latency, thanks to the quad core processor and 2 gb ram. And video streaming is also very smooth. I have only been using this a day, but I haven't had it pause to buffer yet. I have a Chromecast in my son's room, a recent model Mac Mini in the living room, an older C2D Mac Mini in my room with Boxee on it, and a Raspberry Pi, and they all buffer at some point during just about every movie. I stayed in a vacation home with a Roku 2 last summer, and it was great, but it also had to buffer a lot. We also have three game consoles that have streaming video apps, and they buffer, too. I think the Fire's secret may be its wifi card. I am sure that, at some point, my ISP will find a way to slow it down.

So, yeah, I am giving the Fire TV four stars for doing exactly what I need it to do. I had come to Amazon to get another Chromecast, but I saw this and thought it would probably be better suited to what I need in my bedroom (I need my husband to be able to watch a tv show without my help - he is completely tech-challenged and cannot work the Dish remote - too many buttons).

The reason it doesn't get five stars is that there aren't yet enough content apps. There is a manga channel, a documentary channel, an art house channel, along with Crackle and Flixter and Plex (Plex is a for pay service that lets you stream your home content). There is plenty to watch if you are a Prime member (I am - and I appreciated having that already set up on my Fire TV - Thank you, Amazon!) I am also a Dish subscriber, with HBO and a Hopper. I have apps for those directly on some of my devices. I can get them on the internet on the tbs I have hooked up to computers. I can even blast them over to my Chromecast from my tablets. But they aren't on Fire TV, and none of my tablets will screencast to Fire TV. Soon as they are, this is a five star device for me.

I read in Entertainment Weekly that HBO and Amazon Prime have come to an understanding that will make lots and lots of HBO shows available through prime, which will also make them available through Fire TV. For the ones that are not, HBOGO will have an app for this. Between that news and my son's enjoyment of an eight dollar (as opposed to 40 to 60 dollars) platformed on this thing, I am adding a star.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons I’m not a hardcore gamer anymore, so for the past few years, I’ve been using a Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball (thumb trackball). I like trackballs for everyday use, and it’s adequate for casual World of Warcraft playing. Most of the time I just futz around leveling alts or doing 5 mans with friends.

But lately I’ve been wanting a mouse I can customize, with more options to adjust my playstyle. It’s cold in my house in the winter, so I wanted to set up mouseover macros and use more mouse buttons, because my hands are cold sitting on the keyboard. So the G502 Proteus Spectrum seemed like a good mouse to review.

I just had one problem: my computer can’t customize the mouse. Why? I have a Mac Book Air.

Now, I know the G502 says on the box that it supports Windows. There’s no mention of Mac support. But I’ve never had a problem with my Mac recognizing Logitech mice, so I figured I’d be safe. What I didn’t know is that Logitech gaming mice have separate software from the Logitech Control Center for regular Logitech mice.

After some Googling, I found the Logitech Gaming Software, which supports Mac OS X 10.8.x and up. I installed it on a Mavericks machine and a Yosemite machine. Neither computer’s Logitech Gaming Software was able to find the mouse. The G502 Proteus CORE is supported, but not the G502 Proteus SPECTRUM.

So right now, I’m unable to customize any of the extra buttons or RGB lighting or any of the other special features. It’s a really fancy basic mouse. I will continue to check for Proteus Spectrum support in the Mac Logitech Gaming Center, and update this review when I can customize things. I’m going into so much detail on the Mac side of things because I know I’m not the only Mac person who tried to use this mouse. I think there’s a workaround with Bootcamp or using a Windows computer, but I’m unable to try that.

I did use the mouse for a few weeks, to test the comfort. I’m really picky on how mice feel in my hand. I’m female and have smaller hands. I like how this mouse didn’t feel too short, and it wasn’t too heavy or wide for me to use comfortably for hours at a time. I also liked the included weights, so you can adjust the weight of the mouse. I haven’t had a mouse with an adjustable weight before, and I liked that extra level of customization.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons

For the Belkin, I opened the box, plugged into my router, ran a set up program that took less than five minutes, downloaded an app, and I was up and running. While this is a very similar product in both look and function, it took over an hour - and two ethernet cables - to set it up. There is no Mac software on the installation cd. The box states that a Windows pc is required, but the website has a Mac download available. You have to scroll through the product photos, which aren't in alphanumeric order. Just keep looking until you find the DCS-930L - AFTER the 931L and the 932L and the 934L. Have faith. Keep going. It's there.

Once you get the program installed, it takes very little time to *find* the camera and teach it to log into your wireless network. And then you are back to the website to set up your account and view your camera. Except you are on a Mac, and the viewer requires you to install the Java Runtime Environment. JRE is a big old security vulnerability on Macs. So much so that Apple advises against using it. Mavericks lets you turn it on case by case - and, by default, it will ask you every time before running it. If you are on an OS below Mavericks, check the googles for setting your preferences so that you're not running JRE all the time.

Okay, so now you've got JRE going, and the first thing the program tells you is that you have to update your firmware AND you need to have the camera AND your computer ethernet-jacked right into your router. LOLWUT? I'm lucky. I am on a laptop, and I have an extra ethernet cable and an empty port. So, I did that, and there I was, up and running, about an hour, hour and a half, thereabouts, after I started.

Image quality is pretty good - not great. Audio is okay. The settings are very customizable. But the wifi receiver is very weak, and that limits the usefulness of this product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

One day it just stopped charging. I had read dozens of books on there, and had the wifi plus 3g version which was very convenient.

I occasionally read now on the Kindle app on my computer, as I have about 97 books in my library, with probably 15-20 still unread. I noticed on Amazon that there was a promotion...Kindles on sale for Prime members. I thought, you know, it would be nice to read those books I've put off reading because it's just not the same on my computer or phone...I think I'll get another Kindle. I researched reviews for a little while, and decided all I needed was the Paperwhite with Wi-fi. The additional cost for 3G was just not worth it to me...sure, I'd used it before when traveling with my old Kindle to buy a few books, but with a little planning I could've purchased and downloaded the books beforehand. Also, some of the reviews of the higher end Kindles did not impress me.

Anyway, I received the Kindle earlier today. It came almost fully charged, and was so easy to set up. And within minutes had books from my Kindle library loaded! I've been reading for 2 hours straight and so far I love it. I am using it on maximum brightness, sure it may take more frequent charging, but I really love how bright it is and the contrast of the words on the page. I also bought a cover for it and find it is easier to hold IMO. Pages turned with a simple finger swipe.

Hopefully this will last a very long time! I've got so many books I want to read!

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS ZenBook 13 Ultra-Slim Laptop, 13.3” Full HD WideView, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8265U, 8GB LPDDR3, 512GB PCIe SSD, Backlit KB, Fingerprint, Slate Gray, Windows 10, UX331FA-AS51 This review is about what I think >90% of users will care about. The detail specs are a step further, higher and faster and advertised and advertised. The Asus ZenBook 13 has been my go-to everyday toting computer for some 7-8 years.

I have last year’s i5 gen7 ZenBook 13 to directly compare the two.

P.S. This Zen-book has been so good that I had it modified to incorpoarte medical practice compliant HIPA secured software. It's a step function increase in my nightly homework replacing my 7-year old Dell. This laptop is ubiquitously practical with 180 screen twist for descirbing patient procedures. With the med-system handshacks, its like 3x faster than the Dell.

First, this new i5 gen8 ZenBook 13 has a quarter inch all-around smaller footprint. The 1/4" is immediately noticeable from last year’s edition. The 1/4" bezel is noticeably better. As small a footprint as the two have, Asus has reduced the size with no compromise in keyboard utility.

This year's ZenBook is noticeably thinner. Recharge and headphone jack are reversed. This year's hinge is slightly more robust to account for the reduced thickness. The hinge has been a 'should improve' on ZenBooks since inception. This years may solve the issue for good.

The plug-outs are changed. Make sure the output ports are what you want. For my purposes, the addition of a standard HDMI vice last year’s mini-HDMI is an improvement requiring no adapter. Last year’s SD input has been correctly reduced to the increasingly popular/common micro-SD. Plug-out needs are easily resolved with a USB-C adapter hub.

The discrete Nvidia graphics will be an interesting exploration.

The Asus fingerprint reader has never failed. This edition looks identical to last years and has been creatively moved right and off the touchpad. The ZenBook has been the very best reader compared to my HP Envy (dang good) and Dell XPS (50:50 chance).

This year's battery is new tech. The lithium-polymer battery promises up to 14 hours and includes fast-charge technology that takes "just 49 minutes" to recharge to 60% capacity. I get 11 hours out of last year’s battery every day. I can't recall running out of battery on last years on battery save mode on trans-con flights.

Wish it came with Windows Pro instead of Home, but oh well.

Finally, both last years and this year are so fast you'd have to instrument to tell a speed difference. The ZenBooks 1-2-3 second boot to Windows is 'instant' for practical purposes.

Love it. Exceeds expectations. There's no purchase mistake to be made with the UX331.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenBook 13 Ultra-Slim Laptop, 13.3” Full HD WideView, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8265U, 8GB LPDDR3, 512GB PCIe SSD, Backlit KB, Fingerprint, Slate Gray, Windows 10, UX331FA-AS51

If you check Spotify forums, you will find COUNTLESS threads of suggestions for the Spotify app on this watch that should truly be basic features at this price. Do they implement them or listen? No. Also, there is no way to contact Spotify customer service - you just get pointed towards their 'community forum' where you have people complaining of the same exact things with no fix. You can't skip forward on any track, at all. I listen to a lot of podcasts when I walk. Some are 2 hours in length while my walk is only 1 hour. This watch constantly either reverts to the very beginning of my podcast so I have to start all over (because again, you can't skip forward - so have fun listening to ads as well!) in anything, only updates 1 song out of 15 on my playlist or get the error 'sync failed', or some other random issue. Also, if you have a playlist on Spotify, you cannot choose the track you want to listen to. You have to hit the >> button to get to where you want. Really? I hope Garmin drops Spotify because they have been a truly horrible app on this watch the entire time with no effort to make updates. Take a look at the reviews of Spotify on the Garmin store if you don't believe me.
- Battery life is a couple of days. However, there are points in time where my watch will be at say 80% the night before, I get ready to leave and go my walk the next morning, pick up my watch, and it's at 8%. WTF? This happens enough to be super annoying and apparently is not an 'only me' problem. It appears to be tied to when the watch updates.
- I tried to wear this to track my sleep in the beginning and gave up after two nights due to the extreme disco effect of the 'gesture' motions. I tried turning on the 'do not disturb' function advertised on the watch which is supposed to disable this stupidly bright light that WILL wake you and whoever is next to you up. Didn't work. Do a search for 'Garmin watch lights up in middle of the night' and you will find all sorts of people complaining of the same thing, and not just on this version of the watch.
- GPS has issues connecting and can take several minutes which is pretty annoying when you try to start tracking an activity only to see a red bar when trying to connect. I 'sync' my watch to my phone constantly so that is not the issue. I have switched between the GPS options Garmin offers on the watch to no avail. Search for this issue as well and you will see lots of people with the same complaint.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-02172-31 Vivoactive 4S, Smaller-Sized GPS Smartwatch, Features Music, Body Energy Monitoring, Animated Workouts, Pulse Ox Sensors and More, Light Gold with Light Pink Band

text_fidelity_a:
SK hynix Gold S31 1TB SATA Gen3 2.5 inch Internal SSD | SSD 1TB | Up to 560MB/S | Solid State Drive | Compact 2.5" SSD Form Factor SSD | Internal Solid State Drive | SATA SSD Revving up old Macs is like one of my favorite things. I don't do much of it anymore, because (a) arthritis in my hands has made the turning of tiny screws much more of a chore, and (b) I was running out of old Macs.

The last one I had was a 2010 mini that was the first computer I'd bought new since probably 1993 (also a Mac). It had the last of the Core2Duo processors and a spin up hard drive and a couple of gigs of ram that I upgraded pretty much right away. It served as a DVR for a while, then a minecraft server, media streamer, then got put away. I resurrected it to bounce DATS to .WAV to mp3 when I learned that it had digital audio input and output. I had been researching all these expensive things to make that happen, and it turned out that my little friend was able to save me hundreds of dollars with something that had been built in all along.

But it was slow because of the HDD. And upgrading looked really daunting. I'd done one of the earlier minis, and it had been an exercise in anxiety.

But the other day, I decided to give it a try. Two bits of advice: if you can get through this without disconnecting the wifi connector (you can if you are really careful), do so, and (2) if you accidentally disconnect the wifi connector (I did), don't panic. Watch videos of people putting iPhones back together (the older, the better). These connectors are fussy. Do not force them. If they are seated correctly, a light press will connect them. You'll feel the click. But it's almost like threading a needle to get it seated correctly. And if you push too hard, you'll break it. Same with the fan. Just be careful. If you are pushing and it's not connecting right away, it's not lined up right.

Okay, so deciding to do the drive replacement took awhile because the above two steps seemed very daunting. And the project took me several hours, because I had to stop and rest a few times (if your hands work and you keep your screws organized, it should take about 45 minutes). But it was worth every minute.

This is an excellent drive. The form factor lines up exactly with the HDD I pulled from the mini (some of the drives I have used in old white MacBooks and older MacBook Pros have not). Not a millimeter off. The OS install flew. This drive is stellar in this context. If you need a 2.5" SSD, I highly recommend this one.
text_fidelity_b: SK hynix Gold S31 1TB SATA Gen3 2.5 inch Internal SSD | SSD 1TB | Up to 560MB/S | Solid State Drive | Compact 2.5" SSD Form Factor SSD | Internal Solid State Drive | SATA SSD

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

Photos above were taken by the reviewed camera:
- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case
-Second Batman toy image at default resolution, with waterproof case on. Surprisingly, not much difference. Good plastic.

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout These are around the same price as all the junky Chinese wireless earbud brands on Amazon but sound much better, are much more reliable, and are made by a company with good customer service that stands behind their products.

Ankers has several wireless earbuds with the cords that go behind the neck but only these, the spirit, the spirit pro, and the spirit x are worth considering for purchase. Their other earbuds are older models that cost just as much but have less features and weaker specs.

The bass on these is weak but I use these mostly for working out and for that it is fine.

I already have a pair of Apple EarPods but I wanted another wireless pair of headphones as well so I could switch back and forth while the other pair was charging.

These do not work with Apples w1 chip Bluetooth protocol, only apple and beats headphones work with that standard right now so those wireless headphones brands will sound better than anything other wireless headphones will with Apple products.

They also do not have aptx, which is the best sounding Bluetooth standard for anything other than Apple.

Ankers spirit pro headphones do support the aptx standard and supposedly have better bass than these so those are that models advantages.

However the spirit pro cost twice as much as these and only supports Bluetooth protocol 4.1 while these headphones support Bluetooth protocol 5.0.

Why is that important? Because the 5.0 protocol is the new “low energy” Bluetooth standard. Meaning that if you have both a device and headphones that support it you will get much more play time out of the same size battery.

Ankers other most recent model of earbuds, the spirit x headphones, have the same specs as these headphones in terms of the protocols they support but have a different form factor, obviously, and have 10mm drivers while these have 6mm. They also have a little more battery life.

I think I might buy the spirit x headphones as well in order to have a backup and to compare their sound.

As an Apple user the spirit pro headphones are just not worth the extra cost for me since I will never use the aptx protocol and they do not even support the Bluetooth 5.0 protocol.
If they were Bluetooth 5.0 compatible I might consider spending the extra 25 bucks in order to get that extra bass.

While these don’t sound spectacular they will get great battery life when I use them with devices that support 5.0 Bluetooth and they are very affordable.

I want to quickly rant about amazons policies and the flood of cheap Chinese products on here.

If you search for “wireless earbuds” or “Bluetooth earbuds” or any similar terms ankers products will not even show up on the first several pages of results.
Nor will Aukeys headphones, which I think are the second best option for wireless headphones in this price range.

Why is this?
Because the Chinese brands pay “click farms” to leave hundreds or even thousands of 5 star reviews.

The fraud is so obvious. What do you think is happening when a product has more than a thousand 5 star reviews all left on the same day or within the same few days and almost none of those reviews are from verified buyers?
The fact that many of them say the same things over and over and that many of them are written in broken English are other obvious clues.

I reported a few of them but Amazon does not take them down because Amazon cares about money and absolutely nothing else and having millions of people purchase this Chinese junk off their website makes them a lot of money.

It really sucks because good products, like these anker headphones, are barely visible in amazon search results because reputable brands don’t pay click farms to manipulate amazon search results.

It’s the consumers that lose in the end when their headphones, or other cheap Chinese products, break a few weeks after use or maybe never even work to begin with.
And you can bet that half of the time the companies selling this junk on amazon will simply disappear in order to avoid accepting returns and then reappear later under a new seller account to sell more junk through click farm manipulated amazon search results.

Of course amazon will find itself on the hook for some of these costs but apparently the money they make off of allowing all of this Chinese junk to be sold on their website under false practices is much more than any costs they incur.

These practices that amazon allows, and this one issue about manipulated search results is just the tip of the iceberg, hurts not just American consumers it also hurts American companies.

Rant over.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones, Soundcore Spirit Sports Earbuds by Anker, Bluetooth 5.0, 8H Battery, IPX7 Waterproof, SweatGuard, Comfortable Wireless Headphones, Secure Fit for Running, Gym, Workout

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS Transformer Book T100HA-C4-GR 10.1-Inch 2 in 1 Touchscreen Laptop (Cherry Trail Quad-Core Z8500 Processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Windows 10), Gray This is a tablet running a real operating system (Windows 10) hooked up to a small keyboard with a trackpad. And it's all right.

It's thicker and heavier but smaller than my 11 inch MacBook Air, which makes it more convenient in some respects and less convenient in others. The MacBook Air is a used 2012 model with a Core i5 and 4gb ram. It's snappy, but it didn't come with an SD slot, and used it cost about a hundred more than this. The quad core atom processor on the transformer book is pretty fast for a tablet, but it is definitely a lightweight compared to a core i5. Or even an i3.

My iPad Air runs iOS. Way less versatile than Windows 10 in terms of doing work-a-day things, having a browser respond the way you're used to having it respond, etc., but it's still pretty good. However, the keyboard experience is something of a pain, especially since there's no trackpad and you have to touch the tablet face to do the mouse-like things. And using the mail program is harder on the iPad than it is on a mac laptop or on the transformer book.

The transformer book is noticeably slower than either of the other devices, but I was able to do everything I set out to do on it. The Office apps are good and integrate seamlessly with the other Office installations on my other stuff. The screen is as nice as or nicer than my iPad Air. I had a MeMo for a year, and I loved the screen on that. This is very similar - excellent resolution, nice and bright, a bit wider aspect than what the iPad Air has.

The sound is about as good as one would expect. Which is to say, meh. But that's what headphones are for.

Cortano makes it easy to get set up. I asked it to find the apps I wanted. When I want something from the control panel, I ask for that. Since this is my first time with Windows 10, having the assistant helps a lot.

There do seem to be some battery issues. Charging takes a long time. There was an issue with the MeMos, as well, that I sort of resolved by fully cycling the battery a couple of times.

All things considered, I like this tablet/transformer book quite a bit. My only significant issue with it is weight. For my purposes, the ultralight notebook or the regular tablet will meet my needs on any given day. However, if you like your PC desktop and need, essentially, a shuttle craft, though. this is a pretty good compromise machine. It's a decent enough tablet. You can do business stuff, check email, surf the web, and watch movies. You won't be transcoding video or playing resource intense games, but this ultimately is a nice tablet with a keyboard. Not a desktop substitute. Maybe not even a laptop substitute, depending on your needs. But definitely a nice tablet.

UPDATE WITH USAGE ISSUES:

I was getting really annoyed with battery life/charging issues. My iPad Air will stand by for a couple of weeks, no problem, whereas this thing dies if I leave it off the charger a couple of days. It also needs its OEM charger if you intend to charge it within a few hours time, as opposed to overnight and then some. I was able to solve some of this by running task manager and disabling some of the high impact background apps (Microsoft OneDrive is a big offender). And, similar to my other Asus tablet, the battery charging problem seems to improve with conditioning. On the positive side, the more I use this, the better I like it.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS Transformer Book T100HA-C4-GR 10.1-Inch 2 in 1 Touchscreen Laptop (Cherry Trail Quad-Core Z8500 Processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Windows 10), Gray

text_fidelity_a:
CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW) These are pretty much as basic an RCA cable you can find that will extend the length of your existing RCA cables without the need for another male-to-male adapter. While for components that have RCA hookups that allow you to use any RCA cable that your can find, I would recommend buying a single longer cable as every connection point is a place for potential signal loss. However, for components that have their RCA cables integrated with the device, you have little choice but to buy an extender such as this. Turntables, especially the older variety, are the most notable components that have this configuration, and since most people like to be able to play records from a location that is easy to reach and has plenty of headroom, this is often far away from your receiver and the built-in cables on the turntable are usually far too short for this. This is why these cables are a perfect way to add an extra 3' while only introducing one additional connection in your linkage, where using a standard RCA cable with a male-to-male adapter introduces two.

Also, since the cables which are connected to turntables are almost always of bare-bones quality with the minimum gauge of copper necessary to carry a signal (that's assuming the wire is made from copper at all, and not from some other cheaper alloy), these are probably going to be the same gauge. Your connection is only as good as the weakest link, so buying some thick gauge cable that is made out of magnetically polarized copper probably would only serve to drive the price up with no actual benefit to you except for being able to brag about them. Therefore, this RCA cable extenders is all that you really need and will spare you the embarrassment of spending money on something that you actually do not need at all. Some "high end" users might complain about them being of a small gauge because they have convinced themselves that they have to use overpriced Monster cables to connect their gear to be able to fully enjoy it., but I don't necessarily buy into this. True, good cable makes a difference, especially when you are sending a signal over a longer distance (10' or more) chances are the mid-grade cable of 16 gauge copper wire with gold plated contacts is all you're going to need. This cable solves your short cable problem while telling the world "I am care about how my music sounds, but I am neither a sucker nor a fool!"
text_fidelity_b: CablesOnline 6ft 2-RCA Male to 2-RCA Female Red/White Audio Extension Cable, (AV-E406RW)

It comes with a brief, but well-written user guide.

text_fidelity_a: Panasonic LUMIX FZ1000 II 20.1MP Digital Camera, 16x 25-400mm LEICA DC Lens, 4K Video, Optical Image Stabilizer and 3.0-inch Display – Point and Shoot Camera - DC-FZ1000M2 (Black) This is a really nice superzoom camera for those who like to (or have to) travel light. I normally use a 7D Mk ii with various telephoto prime and telephoto zooms for wildlife photography and 5D Mk iv with wide angle prime and zooms for landscape shots. I recently had to go on a trip where it was impossible to bring any of my DSLR kits due to space and weight limitations. I was able get a super deal on a Panasonic FZ-1000 (I guess this is quite an older model at this time). I was somewhat skeptical about the specs at first, but the Leica lens and the 1" sensor performed really well on my test shots, so I decided to take the FZ-1000 as my camera for the trip. The results were surprisingly good. The camera has quick and intuitive user interface, good set of manual controls and several programmable function buttons, so it is relatively easy to learn and set it up to one's preferences. The AF system certainly exceeded my expectations. It did an excellent job of picking subjects behind branches/partial foliage. The success rate for birds in flight was quite good, not nearly as fast or accurate as a 7D Mk ii with EF 400 f/5.6L, but good enough for all practical purposes. Exposure both in scene mode and spot mode (a somewhat large spot) was good. Battery life was also very good. I was getting more than 600 shots per charge using the optical viewfinder and no flash. I did not try the 4K video feature yet, but the 1080p video quality was also very good. The whole package is as big as a low-end DSLR with a kit lens, but gives you 25mm-400mm effective focal range, a relatively fast lens (f/4.0 even at 400mm) plenty of manual control, and a very good AE/AF system. Highly recommended for travel when there is space/weight limitations.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi [Previous Generation] I bought for my mother as a mother's day gift. I also bought a Vera Bradley cover and a $50 Amazon GC to go with it. My mom is not the gadget type. No matter how many times I explain how to change TV setting from the Playstation to the cable box, which for our TV is a one button push, she just cannot do it. So, getting a Kindle was a stretch, however, I wanted her to have the ability to travel without taking a lot of books with her because my mom is also that mom who over packs and has too much stuff, which inevitably means she loses something.

So, the Kindle only gets use when she travel, but she has figured it out somewhat. She can't quite figure out how to purchase books or how to change the settings, which she just gets me to do it for her, but it has gotten a lot of use because she does take it with her instead of a bunch of books. In my use of this Kindle, I find it somewhat clumsy, slow, and some of the icons are not self explanatory and takes a few tries going back and forth. What I do like is that the screen is the exact size of a paperback book, there is no glare whatsoever, which is a problem I have with my iPad, and the light in the screen is perfect for reading at night without a lamp on. The ability to have all of Amazon's e-books at your fingertips is nice if you have a Wi-Fi connection. I don't see a reason to get the 3G as this is just a Kindle for reading only, thus, I and my mother can wait til a Wi-Fi connection is available to download another book if need be. However, you can download multiple books at a time so if you just can't stand not having something to do for 20-30 mins, I would suggest downloading more than one.

Battery life is out of control! I have never seen this go below 50% even after hours of use. One downside is that the plug to charge it is not included so you will have to also pay for that as well. It is also very lightweight, and if you have a little case it's like holding an actual paperback, unlike an iPad which is much heavier and cumbersome to read e-books on.

However, overall, I'm old school. I like paper books. The smell, the ability to write notes and see those notes on the margins, the feel of the paper between my fingers. I can go my references quicker and don't have to worry about running out of memory space because my books stay on a shelf until I need them. So, I recommend this for travel only for the sake making room in your carryon. It is easy to use once you learn all the little quirks. Otherwise, the geek/nerd in me just always goes back to actual black and white.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi [Previous Generation]

text_fidelity_a:
Mudder Portable USB Light Laptop Light for Keyboard Flexible Stick Dimmable Touch Switch LED White Light Lamp for Laptop Computer PC (Black) This is one of those simple but really useful gadgets to have. It's an LED light but, instead of a single bulb or two, it has a row of 10 bulbs arranged in a 6 inch span. The light output at it's brightest level is very bright - actually too bright in that you'll hurt your eyes if you look at the bulbs when they are at full brightness.

You turn the light on by tapping the end of the "bulb stick." Touch once to turn it on/off, press and hold while it is on to adjust the brightness. There's a wide range of brightness levels, from ultra bright to barely on. Unfortunately, it does not remember the last setting when you turn it off and then turn it on again. It always comes on at the brightest setting.

The stalk is very bendy but holds its position well. It's also very sturdy, with a metal rather than plastic casing. The total length is about 19 inches; the bendable stalk about 10.5 inches long. This is very thin - the bulb end is about the width of a pencil - so it's easy to fold up and stow in a tablet or laptop bag. Excellent build quality, especially considering the price.

It has a standard USB connector on the end for power. I've been powering it with a small powerbank and it draws very little power - leaving it on for several hours barely made a dent in the powerbank charge level.

I find this very helpful when using a tablet at night. I can bend the stalk so the light shines where I want it (the attached keyboard) but not on the screen. It's easy to stow when not in use - no wires or bits that get tangled up. Great value for the price.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Mudder Portable USB Light Laptop Light for Keyboard Flexible Stick Dimmable Touch Switch LED White Light Lamp for Laptop Computer PC (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System It took me longer to unpack these than to get music via my iPod Touch streaming through them--the set-up, connecting, streaming process took under about two minutes. Worked fine as well with my laptop.

The sound quality is fine, especially for small speakers. I don't expect them to rattle my windows are pump the base. The lack of a strong bass is noticeable (as mentioned, not a surprise) but I wouldn't call them tinny at all. The sound was quite pleasing and handled high volume with no distortion.

They're small enough to pack or easily move around or outside. They do connect to each other, with detracts from their convenience a bit, and I personally wouldn't have minded a longer connecting cable so as to spread the sound a bit farther apart, but since they're really not made for room-filling sound--aimed more at desktop or otherwise small spaces, it's hard to call that a major complaint or oversight. A longer cable might have pleased me but had others complaining.

I prefer the Creative ZiiSound D3X to these--it's bit more convenient in that it's a single speaker set up and I thought its sound quality a little better, plus it has the ability to add in the subwoofer and other speakers (I have the subwoofer), but really, the difference isn't huge and the intent is somewhat different for most, so these speakers more than suit the bill for their size and purpose.
text_fidelity_b: Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System

Plusses:
+ precise construction

text_fidelity_a: Tenda Wi-Fi Dual Band range extender Let me start by saying I am just a layman so I can’t go into technical issues about this router, if there are any. But I can tell you, as an average person, I love this router. I am using this in lieu of the FIOS router they tried to force on me. it also replaces a pricier TP Link router that failed miserably after 2 weeks. I wanted to be able to cover as much of my house as possible and IF possible eliminate the WiFi extender. This router does that. When I had FIOS installed the line was put in my living room downstairs on the furthest away spot. Great for my entertainment area terrible for my upstairs office on the other side of the house. Which is why I needed an extender for my computer. Now my computer gets almost full signal strength and phenomenal speed. Since my computer only works on 2.4 band speed sucked. With this router I am very close to my 100/100 FIOS speed on the computer! Very happy. Another thing I’ve noticed: when i tried to play 4K content on my TV it constantly buffered. No more. I have been watching 4K with NO issues not even a stutter. Not only do I find the signal strong it is robust enough to handle all my devices (smart electric plugs, blink cameras, computer, phone my Echo and Ech Dot, etc) and it wants more. There’s nothing weak about this router. As for the cons: setup was time consuming. Not impossible but it wasn’t intuitive. I got it done in less than 1/2 an hour but it could have been quicker. The user interface is decent. There are a lot of options. Heck you can even choose the signal strength for each band, and you can set up a VPN. Previously I had to use DD-WRT to do that. Not now. What makes me even happier? The price! Under $60 and I got one heck of a router. I think the material is what I would expect. So no disappointment there. As you see by my pictures my 5.0 band is what I have always gotten: the speed I pay for. BUT my 2.4 signal is much much better (close to the 100 mb I buy) than it had been using “name brand”’routers. I am very pleased I bit the bullet and bought this. I almost didn’t because it’s not a name I know and some reviews were less than glowing. For me this works great and I hope if you buy it you too are pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Tenda Wi-Fi Dual Band range extender

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 The mouse functions fine and I do like the form of it. There is one critical problem though. The form forces the forward and back buttons to be on the opposite side of left and right click so while your thumb is on the forward or back, you have no choice but to squeeze the right or left click to engage the forward/back button. Obviously, this causes inadvertent clicks with the mouse which is a problem. It happens mainly on the forward button as this is where the left and right click start to engage, too (more forward on the mouse itself).

I have not decided if I will keep it or not as I rely heavily on the use of these buttons. If I can find a way to grip it so this does not occur, it will be fine. In the meantime, I'll be using it look for a mouse that is designed better.

UPDATE 2-23-16: Like many others who have posted less than favorable reviews, Anker customer support has reached out to me directly, twice, offering a full refund, which I declined. In my opinion, the mouse works well for it's price, but I stand by the issue noted above. I have gotten used to is and can grip the mouse slightly differently when using the forward button. For this reason and for the outstanding customer service, I have bumped the review to 3 stars and wouldn't hesitate to recommend trying it out given the extremely low risk.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Tablet Mouse for Android 3.1+ You just cannot go wrong with a Logitech mouse, and this one is no exception. Sleek and sexy, well-designed and reliable, this tablet mouse for Android 3.1+ is a joy to hold. I love the color, too. It reminds me of my beloved old teal Logitech corded mouse that wouldn't work with the newer computers. This is a notebook-sized mouse, which is the size I prefer. It is not as tiny as some of the little mice out there, though. Not too big, not to small; just right.

Logitech stresses that this is an Android mouse and that it's not going to work properly with anything older than Android 3.1. It's even in the product title, so it's obvious that the OS is important, but I'm sure there will be people out there who will think it's going to work with earlier versions of Android. I wouldn't chance it. Some other reviewers have reported successfully pairing this mouse with non-Android systems, but I haven't been able to. It did happily meet and greet a friend's tablet PC, however.

Note that, unlike some Logitech mice, this mouse does NOT have a dongle, so you must have a bluetooth-enabled machine to use it. I tried it with a generic bluetooth dongle on my Windows Vista laptop, and I couldn't get it to work. That's not the mouse's fault. One good thing about it is that you can use it with a bluetooth keyboard; if I were going to get one, I'd go with Logitech's keyboard so I know they'll play nice.

I haven't had the opportunity to run down the batteries of this mouse, but if this one is like the other Logitech mice I own, the batteries last a long, long time--unlike competitors' mice, which seem to chew up and spit out batteries every few weeks. You can turn the mouse off, of course, but the sleep function also conserves batteries. Very nice.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Tablet Mouse for Android 3.1+

It is very comfortable. The wrist wrest is a nice bonus. It is a very large keyboard and takes up a lot of desk space, which may not be for everyone. Because the keyboard is so large, the mouse has to be kept considerably far to the right of the user, and this is not ergonomic. There are lots of additional media and keys of various functions, however, I think some of these could have been hidden under an alternate function layer to save space. Some people don't like that though and that is a matter of preference.

The keystroke action is comfortable for a rubber dome type board, but if you strike the key on the edge, which is very easy to do because of the different heights of the keys, the key is very stiff and doesn't wanna go down. I am a better typist now than I was then but it interfered enough with typing that I had to get a different board. If you are the type of person who doesn't always strike the keys dead center this is something to consider.

ASUS Chromebook C425 Clamshell Laptop, 14" FHD 4-Way NanoEdge, Intel Core m3-8100Y Processor, 8GB RAM, 64GB eMMC Storage, Backlit KB, Silver, Chrome OS, C425TA-DH384 First off this works perfectly for what I wanted it for... sitting on the couch, relaxing, while the TV is on. I do not use this for work or gaming, I have a desktop for that. I was using a tablet, but honestly I hate it. I just can't adjust to typing on a touch screen, I want a real keyboard. I also hate fingerprints on my screen. I deal with it on my phone, but for a larger screen it makes me crazy. So I figured this would be a good solution, when it popped up for review. It fits comfortably on my lap and the screen is small enough I can see over it to watch tv, but large enough it is easy on my eyes. So far its been great, although I miss the left and right mouse buttons built into the touch pad area of most laptops. Maybe its a Chromebook thing, but I will just have to adjust.

I will say though it does feel a bit flimsy. I like the lightness, but in my lap typing I can feel the plastic body flexing. For the price I'd expect something a bit more durable, at least for the bottom half with the keyboard. The keys are responsive, although I'm use to my mechanical keyboard so switching to the thin chiclet style makes them feel mushier than they probably are. For a small laptop, they don't feel cramped and they are raised enough that I'm not miss-typing.

It was incredibly easy to set up, just entered my google log-in info and poof I was up and running. This would be a 5 star product if they hadn't just made it a bit sturdier.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS Chromebook C425 Clamshell Laptop, 14" FHD 4-Way NanoEdge, Intel Core m3-8100Y Processor, 8GB RAM, 64GB eMMC Storage, Backlit KB, Silver, Chrome OS, C425TA-DH384

text_fidelity_a:
Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray This Honeywell smart home security starter kit has a great video and is easily expandable.

When opening the box I was pleased to see that it was packaged very well. The box even has a magnetic closure. Maybe a little over the top but a nice feature to make it feel like more of a luxury product. I also have the Honeywell thermostat and that box wasn’t as nice.
Each item in the security kit was simple and clear to find since they were labeled in their own little box. There is an instruction sheet that is quite large for the info that it holds. The instructions have nice graphics and it is spaced out well so it is very easy to read. The instructions are simple for initial set up. Though I would appreciate another manual to help with the “extra” things it can do. I relied on the Honeywell videos and reviews (video and written) by other people to get it functioning with all the bells and whistles. I could see the need for a manual for those less tech savvy.

The base station could be a little smaller but it looks very nice in my kitchen and blends in very well. It’s a nice design with only one button, for the speaker. You can touch the top to check how it is working and run your finger around the top to change the volume. The camera is small and has a privacy ring that can be twisted to block the camera. It would be a nice feature if I could twist the camera from the app in case we forgot to open it when we left.
The middle mesh part is the speaker and it has a good range of volume and the sound is good.
The bottom has a light inside and it changes colors when you choose the different settings. It also lights up to help when you set up new devices.
The base has a backup battery. You will get an alert when it doesn’t have power. This has been handy when there is a storm so I know when the power goes out and when it is restored.

To start the set up I downloaded the Honeywell app. It was easy to use and is a nice looking app. The main page is very simple. When you go to the settings that’s where all the extras are.
My husband also has the app on his phone so he can use it just as I can.
Set up was very easy besides having troubles with it connecting it to my WiFi. I decided to wait till the next day and it worked after a couple tries. I don’t have a fast internet so that might be why. I haven’t had any issues with the connection since set up. Besides the WiFi wait it was about 15 minutes to set up the app and base.
The key fob was very easy to pair up and only took me a couple minutes to have it ready to use. Nice to have when a babysitter comes over.
The access sensors were very easy to install and set up. I didn’t need the extra piece. It only took me a few minutes to stick them on and pair them. I did use painters tape to attach them to my doors and frames. I am worried about the tape they have ruining my stained trim. I haven’t seen any comments about it. I also wanted to try it on other doors and windows first.
When you open a door or window in home mode it chimes and sends you an alert. When you open in away mode it will sound the alarm. I wish the door sensors were a little smaller or gray. They stand out too much on my wood trim and door. If my trim was white they wouldn’t be very noticeable.

The camera is very clear and has a wide angle so if you position it right you can see a lot. You can switch the video to full screen and the picture is still good. You are also able to zoom in on the video in the app and it has options to take a snap of the video, talk through the base or have an alarm go off. Sometimes it takes a while for the video to load or it will just turn off. I am assuming this is from my slower internet. Usually after a few tries I can get it to work. Also there is a delay in the video and the movement is jumpy, this could be due to the slower internet also. You still get a good picture of who is there. I was impressed with the night vision.

The motion detection is a nice feature when you are away. I have been trying to figure out the best setting while we are at home. It will send me alerts all the time when we are home. Most of the alerts are during the people detection time. Maybe because our camera covers so much of our main area. I do like that how the people detection can let me know who is in the house and I don’t have to look at the video. When it detects motion it will take a short video clip and save them below the live video. You can scroll down to look at the older ones. It looks like the clips are saved for a day. The people detection is limited to 2 hours. But I did notice that you could set it for the morning then when that time was over you could change it for later in the day. You would have to remember to change it but good to know if you wanted it on for longer or multiple times in the day. Not sure why they don’t have an option for more time.

The geofencing didn’t work well for me. It would switch to away mode even when the phone was close to it. We’ve decided to turn that feature off. It’s easy enough to turn it to away with the app, key fob, or talk to it. We are at home a lot so it makes more sense to do it manually. But I could see it being a great feature for people gone more during the day.

The kids like the Alexa feature that it comes with. They can ask the weather, time, kids jokes. I use it for the timer and to ask it questions. We had problems with playing songs. It wanted us to subscribe to amazon music. We have found other ways of playing music but it’s not very easy. Alexa seems limited but still useful. This is my first Alexa enable device so hard to compare.

I like that the security base links to my Honeywell thermostat (it was very easy to pair it) and I can tell Alexa to turn it off or change the temperature or use the same app. I would like to get other devices that link to it. This is a great starter kit and I like that it is expandable for your needs.

You are able to do two way taking with the app. It’s not always easy to understand and you have to talk slower.

The box says you get free 24-hour cloud storage. I’m not sure if that’s for the video clips or what you are actually storing. I haven’t found where the cloud is accessed.

Overall it is easy to use and looks nice. It’s nice that you can have a security system that is easy to use and it doesn’t have a monthly fee. I don’t usually need all the security features that this security system offers but it’s nice to have it set up and ready for when I do.
text_fidelity_b: Honeywell Home Smart Home Security Starter Kit, gray

USB C Docking Station, UtechSmart 18in1 Quadruple Display Laptop Docking Station for MacBook Pro & Windows,Thunderbolt 3 Dock with SSD Enclosure 3HDMI VGA 100WPD 5USB-A SD/TF Slot 3.5mm RJ45 Everything about this dock is either confusing, misleading, or falsely. First of all, I’m not quite sure I see the point of having two hosts connect to it as I it does not seem to be a like a KVM switch in any way. For one, video output is dedicated to one or the other host depending on the port. There is no switch to toggle between hosts so USB devices seem to be shared? Honestly it’s not at all clear. The power supply also can only charge one host, I believe whichever is plugged in first. Since there is a single ethernet jack that both hosts share it also shares a single MAC ID. The only explanation for any of this seems to be to give a buyer some impression that it behaves like a KVM switch that allows you to share peripherals. In fact it’s not even clear what it does as the instructions are incomplete. Since I was unable to get a keyboard to work connected to it I presume can you either use the built-in keyboard or plug it directly into the laptop.

I honestly didn’t even fully unboxed this thing after reading the instructions and trying to make sense of them. Once I saw that video was not shared and that the resolution was appallingly low, all of the other issues were already moot. It is advertised as a thunderbolt 3 dock but it’s apparent that thunderbolt 3 support is quite limited and it’s really a USB-C dock. Seeing how the function of this device is very unclear a pure its existence only serves to fool customers like me into not having to use a KVM. Since the description and the instructions appear to be deliberately vague, it would seem this is the point. This also explains why it’s so much less expensive than a single host dock or a dual host KVM.

Back to Amazon with you!
text_fidelity_b: USB C Docking Station, UtechSmart 18in1 Quadruple Display Laptop Docking Station for MacBook Pro & Windows,Thunderbolt 3 Dock with SSD Enclosure 3HDMI VGA 100WPD 5USB-A SD/TF Slot 3.5mm RJ45

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones, Anbes Wireless Earbuds, IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earphones with Ear Hooks & Mic, HD Stereo in-Ear Headphones Gym Running Workout, 8 Hours Battery Noise Canceling Headsets When I first got these, I had a problem with the left earpiece not having sound, and the sound that came from the right ear was very tinny. Customer service was absolutely wonderful to resolve this for me very quickly. Since then, the sound is great! I have really small ears and I do find them a bit too big, even with the smallest cover, which keeps me from wearing them as long as I'd like. I haven't actually tried them in wet conditions, so I can't speak to this, but they are very well made and seem like they will last a long time.
--Pros
*Even though I was worried about the earpieces not being switchable, because I am left eared, this has worked alright when I am driving. I just hang the left earpiece on my shirt and use it with my right hand to work the controls.
*Charging is very fast.
*A charge last quite a long time, especially if you only use them for calls. Even listening to music it last a long time.
*The sound is nice and loud with lots of bass for listening to music.
*Call sound quality is great, for me, and for the listening party.
*The are easy to keep up with, using the nice case that they came with. It slips right into my purse or other bag.
*Well made. Durable and made with quality materials.
---Cons
*The earpieces are too large for my ears, even with the smallest cover, and my ears start to hurt after a short time.
*The pieces that go around your ears is shaped in a way that the bottom pushes into the back of my ear, causing it to get very sore.
*They are a bit larger and heavier than I'd like them to be.
*It would be nice to have a small clip for when you are driving, so that you can clip it to your shirt, to be hands free.

Overall, these are great headphones. They need a little tweaking, especially on the earpieces to make them more comfortable on the ears, but I would still highly recommend them.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones, Anbes Wireless Earbuds, IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earphones with Ear Hooks & Mic, HD Stereo in-Ear Headphones Gym Running Workout, 8 Hours Battery Noise Canceling Headsets

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player When we first tried it, the streaming was awful. It couldn't hold a connection to Vudu, to Hulu, or to Netflix.

We ran an update--tricky because it didn't readily hold a solid network connection--and things improved considerably. I can stream Hulu with minor hiccups, Netflix without issues, and Vudu except at 1080p. For the record, I can stream Vudu at 1080p on the TV that the player is connected to. It still supports only a small subset of services, though Hulu has been added. As a streaming media player, it doesn't meet expectations. As a simple blu-ray player, it is quite excellent for the price. It was able to play a few old, slightly scratched DVDs that other players were having trouble loading.

On the signature features, I could find no appreciable difference in boot up or launch time between this and my Sony, or between this with fast boot turned on and this with fast boot turned off. Blu-ray players tend to boot pretty fast in any case. This one allows up to four users to have customized interfaces, but it only affects the background image and color scheme of the interface screen. It does not allow four users to each maintain their own login to Netflix or Hulu, which would be useful if Netflix ever allowed multiple users of an account to maintain their own Watch Instantly queue the way they do with DVD queues.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMP-BD87 Ultra-Fast Booting Blu-ray Disc Player

Window Alarm 4 Packs - Loud 120dB Alarm and Vibration Sensors Compatible with Virtually Any Window - Glass Break Security Alarm Sensor- Low Battery LED Indicator [[VIDEOID:b48bc2e7b26de5db60ee82130080df8d]] So here’s the deal. These things are a great addition to any home security system, or a great deterrent if this is the only security you have. Most home break in thrives do not want to be seen or heard. They also know there is no way to beat a stand alone window break sensor. If they see this in your front window they are just going to go somewhere else. And to me the blinking led is the best feature of this device. It’s a beacon to the thieves saying “I will hear you”.

So how does it work? I have added a video showing me measuring the sound levels compared to the claims. My meter measured 115DB right next to the unit. That’s close enough to call the claim accurate. The video also shows the sound dissipation as you move away. The sound level is cut in half at about 10 feet. But unless you are a very heavy sleeper wearing earplugs, you are probability going to hear this go off in the dead of night.

The fact that you get 4 for 25.00 is just icing on the cake. Put two facing the street In very visible places and two in the back on your sliding doors or windows. I am probability going to get another 4 to cover the rest of my windows. This is really a good product and I would definitely recommend it.

FYI: I paid full price for this product and was not given any consideration for this review. In fact I search for “window break sensor” here on amazon and this showed up. Glad I found it. If you found this review helpful please indicate so below.
text_fidelity_b: Window Alarm 4 Packs - Loud 120dB Alarm and Vibration Sensors Compatible with Virtually Any Window - Glass Break Security Alarm Sensor- Low Battery LED Indicator

Bose SoundTrue around-ear wired headphones II - Apple devices, Navy Blue When I shop for headphones, I shop primarily for comfort. I’m not a sound snob -- I just need headphones that are super comfortable.

I’ve had a few pairs of over-ear/around-ear headphones. If I wear them too long, they give me a headache, either because they are too heavy after a while or squeeze too much or both. My last was a pair of Skullcandy’s, Hesh style, and I couldn’t wear them for more than 2-3 hours. These Bose SoundTrue’s feel a little lighter, and the ear cups are oval, not round, which makes them fit me better. They also don’t feel as tight on my head as the Skullcandy’s, but I don’t feel like they’re going to fall off.

Soundwise, I think they’re fine. But as I said, I’m not a sound snob, so as long as music sounds good and not like it’s played through a tin can, I’m happy.

Convenience wise, the ear cups swivel so the headphones fit in the included flat case. They don’t fold up a lot, but the case will be handy for when I want to take the headphones out with me. The cord is detachable, and has a remote for music/phone call control. I received the Apple version to review, so only the play/pause worked on my phone, but the other functions worked on my Macbook Air.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTrue around-ear wired headphones II - Apple devices, Navy Blue

text_fidelity_a: Tile Mate (2016) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer The title is good at doing what it does, that being said, it's not a complete life changer. I bought both the wallet and key finder for someone who loses everything everywhere. It's very convenient when the item is simply lost in the house. I believe it would be nicer if everyone in the world used a tile so that the software would be able to constantly locate a missing item but that's just not the case. However, we did lose a wallet in someone's car after being dropped off at home. The app last located the item at the house which was the last time the phone and wallet were together. After asking the person to look in there car, they were unable to find it. But one day when the phone was near that same car it was able to pick up the signal coming from the tile and we ended up finding it wedged deep down between the seats. That being said, if someone were to steal your item, it's probably not going to help but the way the tile works in telling you its last location is super useful.

The monitor has built-in speakers, so I can hear a game’s music while playing. It’s a small but nice feature; I can easily switch the input from my laptop to my Switch and not have to rearrange my whole desk to play games.

The picture is bright and vibrant. I’ve been playing Hades for the last month and it looks SO good on this screen. Bright and crisp, even if I play during the day. The power cable is relatively short, only 50 inches. It’s an AC adapter, not a power brick. The box also includes an HDMI cable -- another nice plus -- but unfortunately my cable had a cut in the coating, so I could see the copper wire.

Overall, I think this is a decent budget monitor. I never want to play my Switch in handheld mode anymore, the picture quality has spoiled me that much. The dual HDMI inputs make it easy to switch between work and fun; I’ve also used this as a Discord display, rotated 90° on a VESA arm.

Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless) I am probably one of the least intuitive people around when it comes to technology. I've bought quite a few gadgets that have ended up collecting dust as I never really learned to use them properly. My short lived relationship with a Palm Pilot ended in frustration when I didn't learn how to back it up on my PC and all my carefully inputted data was lost (more than once!) My kids use it now for a doodle pad. My husband says I have a "black thumb" when it comes to anything electronic. If there is a way to break it, lose it, or misuse it, I'm right there doing it. This is why it is so astonishing that I have grown to love my kindle 2.

I learned how to use it easily within a few minutes. It is so intuitive- my four year old enjoys it and can page back and forth reading classics such as George MacDonald's The Princess and The Goblin or Mary Pope Osborne's The Magic Treehouse. My tween age son uses it for Shakespeare- I downloaded the First Folio (35 plays from the Bard) for all of 99 cents! It's quite a favorite amongst my children and I have recently learned that if more than one family member has a kindle, all e-books may be shared with a single purchase. My friend can even access her kindle books and magazines from her iphone!

Cool features include 6 different options for font size, and text markers by "location" to bring you to the same line of text whether you use the biggest or smallest of fonts, as page numbers would vary too much to be useful. A male or female voice can read to you, though the voices are a bit stiff and robotic, and they make small mistakes such as using alternate pronunciation that don't fit context with heteronyms such as read/read or live/live. You can connect speakers or earbuds/headphones for this feature. Magazines can be downloaded as a single issue or a subscription, but the subscriptions cannot be canceled from the kindle- the user must go to amazon's "Manage my kindle" area to do this.

I have downloaded quite a few classic books for free and spent about a dollar on many others. So far, the younger children's literature has been somewhat limited, but I imagine that as prices drop, more will become available. I am a bibliophile and I never thought I would love a paper book replacement, but this device is so clean and glare free that I forget I am not looking at a paper page.

I'm sure that color kindles will be available within a few years, to make the illustrations a bit more interesting. I love the beautiful pen and ink type renderings which fill the kindle 2 screen when it isn't in use. Obviously though, color would be more attractive with other types of art. Black and white is easiest on the eyes for text, and mostly that it what kindle is all about.

The kindle 2 holds a charge for a long time. I think I plug mine in about once every couple of weeks. If you are not careful with the five way button, sometimes you do end up getting the wrong result. I purchased a book accidentally this way, but amazon has a handy "did you purchase this by mistake?" option which permits you to cancel the order if you act right away.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless)

text_fidelity_a:
Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models) Overall, this is a fine case for the 8.9 inch Fire HD. The overall quality is quite nice - I have other Marware products for my Kindle Touch, and it's good to see that they are continuing to maintain a strong focus on product quality. All the materials feel nice; the stitching is tight and even; there's ample cushioning for tablet protection while maintaining a slim profile; and the elastic strap holds the cover closed in a secure fashion.

I also like how Marware packages their products with a minimum of packaging waste but still ensures the product can travel through the mail without being dinged up. The package is also easy to open - no fuss, no muss.

I initially had some difficulty getting the Fire into the case. The Fire is held in place using a plastic cradle, but it seemed to be too small. I had to (gasp!) resort to reading the user guide that came with it, and found out I needed to position it in a certain way and then snap it in. When it is properly inserted you'll hear and feel a clear "snap" at each of the four corners of the tablet. When properly installed the case holds the tablet very securely. I shook it vigorously (over a thick cushion in case it failed) and the Fire stayed put.

My main quibble is with the rotation feature. I was really looking forward to this since some apps only run in portrait mode; others only in landscape. While the rotation feature works, it is very stiff - you really have to twist hard to get it to rotate. It's a two-handed operation: one hand to rotate the tablet; the other to hold the case while you're turning.

The bottom of the cradle has a tab that fits into a slot on the base of the cover to prop up the tablet. This works in both landscape and portrait modes. There are three tabs so you can adjust the angle.

There are cut outs for the power and HDMI ports. I had no problems accessing any of the ports, power button or volume controls while it was in the cover.

Since I often end up having to charge the Fire while it is in use, I rotated the screen so the power plug is at the top. That allows me to keep the tablet propped up on my desk in landscape mode for video watching, but still use the power cord.

It also offers an auto on/off ability - the Fire turns off when you close the cover, and wakes up when you open the cover. It's a nice feature and it works well.

It has a slot on the cover so you can fit your hand into it for ease of holding it. That has value, but what I would have preferred to have instead (or in addition to) is a pocket on either the inside or the outside to hold items such as a cleaning cloth. This is not a huge problem, but I'll certainly miss that since the case for my original Fire has a outside pouch that is great for holding a cleaning cloth and a small stylus.

I'm going to give this 5 stars, but 4.5 is more accurate given the reluctance of the rotation feature. But, since it does everything else very well, looks good, and feels nice, it's closer to a 5 rating than a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models)
