I primarily use my computer to illustrate books for my day job, and this screen really makes my illustrations look great! Set to "Graphics" mode (rather than "Entertain" mode) the colors are true and the shadows retain great detail; the highlights are smooth, and clean. The color profile is easy to adjust. I really appreciate all of this very much. In the "Entertain" mode, the colors are amped up and the graphics are sharpened, etc. This is nice for watching films and gaming, but for doing graphics work it's absolutely necessary to have the colors and details represented accurately. The excellent anti-reflection and anti-glare features are also extremely helpful in this regard.

The native speakers are about what you would expect; they aren't amazing, but they aren't really all that bad for what this TV is intended to be either. It's really all about the screen. I personally don't care too much about the speakers, because 95% of the time that I use the screen I'm wearing headphones anyway so that I don't disturb my family. But if you're a real audiophile and that sort of thing is important to you, I would suggest you get some nice speakers to go with the TV, because the built-in speakers are clearly only meant to be just good enough to pass muster, and aren't anything to be wowed by.

For me, it's really nice that it doubles as a picture frame when I'm not actively using it for anything else. I have loaded an assortment of my own favorite photographs and illustrations for it to cycle through, and they look really great on this screen, but you can also access a fairly good assortment of art through the TV itself. This turns what is typically a bit of an eyesore in my opinion (I don't like the intrusive look of too much electronic technology in my home) into a lovely, active decoration instead.

I have not ordered a decorative frame to customize it; the reviews on those seem to indicate that they are perhaps overpriced and fragile, and I think it would be easy enough to make my own anyway, which I plan to do. I think having a frame on it would just be the cherry on top, so to speak.

And to reassure anyone who is wondering about the review that said this is the 2021 model, I think there must have been some confusion on one end or the other, because I definitely received the 2022 model that I ordered.

It came with the "Slim-Fit Wall Mount" included in the box (it's in the Styrofoam packing; I think another reviewer might have just not seen it, as it's not very large and it weighs much less than you might expect) along with a decent length of "One Invisible Connection" cable to attach it to the "One Connect Box" controller. This cable is just silver braid with a clear coating on it to help it blend in better than a regular black plastic cable. It serves as a power source as well as controlling the TV, so there's no bundle of unsightly cables hanging down from the screen.

The connect box replaces the usual bulk of the TV, which is what allows the screen to hang so flat on the wall like a regular picture frame. To use the TV, you'll need to position the One Connect box where you can use the remote to control it. It can be positioned anywhere so long as it's within reach of the cable. You can buy longer "One Invisible Connection" cables if necessary. The one that was included was long enough for my needs.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model)

Open the box and you'll find attractively packaged (hint hint to someone thinking of getting these as a gift) headphones as well as a round case with a zipper matching the color. Inside are an assortment of 3 additional sets of eartips, a small, large (the medium is already attached) and a flanged for deep ear insertion. Then I compared them to my old but loved Lady GaGa Monster Beats, as well as a few lower end headsets. Granted the Beats are getting a little wonky, but I have to say it's better to be in the MEE EDM Universe. Can't help but notice logo similarity, hmmmm.

My mother was great lover of opera and symphony. I grew up listening to her records, and when I was small I'd ask her to put on Ravel's Bolero and I'd lie down, listening to it build.
Need to get out of your skin for a while? Put these on, lie down flat on your back. Hit play, close your eyes, palms up, and just absorb everything.

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black) When I installed my Blink XT2, I found I needed to move it a little lower so I could maybe see the face of the delivery person. Thinking I could unscrew the mount without removing the camera, I turned the camera to one side so I could access the screws. The camera fell to the floor. A little bit of friction is not sufficient to hold these cameras. That is when I started looking at these mounts which SHOULD be included in the box.

This is in several parts. Plastic camera-enclosing parts are held together with 4 small screws. The metal part is attached to the wall with 3 flat-head #6 screws.

Unscrew the adjusting part so the base of the mount can be attached to the wall. Do not try to adjust the angle unless this part is loose. Use care when tightening the screws - do it manually so the screws are not over-tightened. The aluminum base could be cracked by over-tightening.

The small screws that are used to attach the back cover to the front should be machine screws, and the posts into which they are screwed should be metal. This is my opinion and is because these screws will have to be removed and reinstalled every time the batteries are replaced.

One piece of plastic had a small 'tab' on it that had to be cut off before the back cover would attach to the front.

A hole in the bottom of the plastic is there to allow a charging cable to be attached. If you do not plan to use rechargeable batteries and have no need for the USB cable, plug the hole so insects do not go inside looking for a new home. I used a small piece of closed cell foam packing material (photo).

If you want to use these mounts with the earlier Blink cameras, you might want to use some foam so the camera does not move around inside the enclosure (photo).
text_fidelity_b: Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Audio-Technica ATH-M50xBT2 Wireless Over-Ear Headphones, Black I plan to start recording music of my own at home. So, I've been researching everything I'd need. A decent pair of monitor headphones are at the top of the "essential" list. I figured that if I were going to be spending money on some headphones, I'd like them to work casual use as well as mixing. So, after lots of digging, reading reviews, watching comparison videos, I have determined that the M50x would be the best for me, for the following reasons:

* Excellent sound quality
* Relatively flat response rate
* Comfortable with glasses
* Detachable cables (included with purchase)
* Reasonably affordable

I'm glad I put in all the legwork ahead of time. These arrived yesterday, and I've worn them for several hours, listening to music (mostly rock, metal and pop) and playing games (Diablo 3 and Skyrim.) The sound quality is outstanding. Admittedly, these are the first studio monitors I've listened to. I've owned decent "fun" headphones in the past (~$50 range) and these are by far superior to what I've experienced.

It took me a bit to settle on these, as some folks claimed that they were either bass heavy, harsh, or uncomfortable. Fortunately, I've found none of this to be true. I've had these on for up to 2 hours with no discomfort what-so-ever. When it comes to the sound, all I can say is "wow!" Everything is extremely clear, and I feel, balanced. The bass is definitely there, but it's not overpowering, and it certainly doesn't detract from other frequencies. The high end comes in really well, and not harsh at all to me. The layers in the music I've listened to so far are so much easier to distinguish.

In the past, I've been able to accurately distinguish various bitrate MP3s/audio files over laptop speakers (128 vs 256 vs lossless.) These headphones make it way easier.

Update - I've recently tried 2 other sets of headphones that my be somewhat comparable: Rockville Pro M50's and the Sony WHCH710N. The M50x's are by far better than both. The Rockville headphones are 1/3 the price and actually pretty close, if you take the price into comparison. The Audio Technicas are a fair amount clearer with nicer highs and lows. The Sony headphones were fairly disappointing, and I wouldn't recommend them, unless you needed wireless. I'm still very happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Audio-Technica ATH-M50xBT2 Wireless Over-Ear Headphones, Black

Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver

So I chose this one instead, and I'm happy I did. This little tripod is very stable. And when you have the legs folded together it makes a nice pistol grip for your pocket camera, something I don't think the wobbly segmented kind would do well.

The velcro strap is about a foot long, which means it will wrap around just about anything the bendable tripods will, and, I think, holds the camera much more safely and securely.

The head tightens nicely and doesn't slip. I tried the tripod with a Panasonic DMC-ZS3, which is fairly heavy as far as pocket cameras go, and it held securely without a bit of slip in the mounting head.

And it really is very light.

The plugable dock is truly a great fit during this home-work environment.

text_fidelity_a:
Etymotic Research MC5 Noise-Isolating In-Ear Earphones I bought these to supplement my ER6i phones which I enjoy and have had no problems with. Unfortunately, they are no longer made so I bought these which I felt would be equivalent. That turned out to not be the case. The sound isolation is lacking, no matter how far they are jammed into my ear canals - it seems they may be purposely letting in some med/high end frequencies to give the phones a more open sound. In my case it seems to heighten certain ambient noises I am interested in blocking - running fans especially. Microphony from the dangling cables seems to be more noticeable too.

These guys have to absolutely invade my ear canals whereas the ER6i phones would need to just barely enter my ear to make a seal. The result is very noticeable and eventually uncomfortable.

The wires are thicker which seems nice at first, but they just get in the way - the thinner wires of the ER6i would pretty much fall into place and not be a nuisance.

All in all, I could tell these were unacceptable within a half hour of use and they are going back.
text_fidelity_b: Etymotic Research MC5 Noise-Isolating In-Ear Earphones

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF 24-105mm f/4 L IS USM Lens for Canon EOS SLR Cameras The Canon 24-105mm f/4 L lens with Image Stabilization is a fantastic lens for those times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. The range on this lens takes you from a decent wide angle perspective to a mid-range telephoto without any light loss (the maximum aperture is constant throughout the zoom range) and image stabilization keeps focus problems due to hand shake well away.

Optical quality is excellent, as you would expect with an L lens, and autofocus is smooth and fast. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @40-170mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 24-105mm f/4 L IS USM Lens for Canon EOS SLR Cameras

RapidX Mini PD 30W USB Type-C PD Wall Adapter - White This charger has the same size prongs on both end so it will fit into an outlet either way.
This charger doesn’t come with a cable but works fast!
I charged my iPhone XR starting at 41% - it went up 28% in 20 minutes!
I also charged my iPhone XS starting at 38% - it went up 35% in 29 minutes!
In around 45 minutes my iPhone XS was up to 85%.
My iPhone XR got a little warm while charging but nothing out of the norm. I didn’t feel any heat when charging my iPhone XS.
I did notice that with the new iOS once my phone hit around 90% the speed at which it charged was a lot slower.
The prongs on this charger do no fold down.
